objective: Determine whether frozen H67 ep35 FFN and attention weights already contain exact 16/32-channel groups that hardware can skip, and quantify only fail-closed low-energy pruning sensitivities otherwise.

result.interpretation: The frozen checkpoint has no exact structured group skip and no unusually low-energy tail: removing 25% or 50% of the least-energy paired groups removes almost the same fraction of weight energy. Structured skip therefore requires explicit retraining and valid825 guardrails.

algorithm_feedback.ffn: If pursued, train a shared 16/32-channel pair mask that removes each fc1 output row group and the corresponding fc2 input-column group together; start with stage 2 and freeze a valid825 AEE/event-rate guardrail before training.
algorithm_feedback.attention: Do not implement a new Q/K/projection skip datapath from the frozen checkpoint. A shared Q/K/projection group mask must first be trained and evaluated; attention Amdahl remains secondary.

paper_safe_statement: The frozen H67 ep35 checkpoint contains zero exact 16/32-channel paired FFN groups and zero exact shared Q/K/projection groups in both float and canonical INT8. Low-energy group removal is nearly proportional to channel removal and is a training sensitivity, not an admitted hardware speedup.
